title: The trail
steps: The trial is over, and in the hall there are three creatures that did not exist this morning. Orla closes the book: "Look after them. What your familiar sees, you see. And its name, only to those you truly love." And she goes down to fetch the next class.
{familiar} will not leave {friend}'s pocket alone, and {friend} cries out: "Hey! That's where I keep the box of threads."

The creature shoots across the hall like an arrow and slips into a tiny arch at the foot of the wall. You can hear it moving inside the wall. It comes back carrying something: a black thread, with the same knot.
I've read about it. The castle is full of small passages: they were made so that familiars could carry messages from one room to another. A person doesn't fit. Not even us.
Whoever knotted the brooms keeps thread in there.

"And if we know where, it's no longer three threads in a box," says {friend}. You go down a floor. In the corridor under the hall, at the foot of the wall, the passage has another mouth, small as a cat flap. Inside, by the light of your wand, another thread.
Not even my head fits. {familiar} does.
